title: Impact of Political Turnover on Public Spending

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
We will use an instrumental variable (IV) approach to estimate the causal effect of Democratic control on public spending. The instrument, z (close-election Democratic win), is used to account for potential endogeneity in x (Democratic control). The key assumption for this approach is that the instrument is relevant (i.e., it affects the endogenous variable, x) and exogenous (i.e., it is uncorrelated with the error term in the structural equation).

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(AER)
library(lmtest)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s74_data.csv")

# Run the first-stage regression (IV regression)
first_stage <- lm(y ~ x + z + controls, data = data)

# Run the second-stage regression (2SLS)
second_stage <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = data)

# Print the coefficient of x (Democratic control) from the second-stage regression
print(coef(second_stage)["x"])

# Basic robustness checks
# 1. Test for relevance of the instrument
F_test <- linearHypothesis(second_stage, "z = 0")
print(F_test)

# 2. Test for exogeneity of the instrument (using the Sargan test)
sargan_test <- vif(second_stage)
print(sargan_test)

# 3. Test for heteroskedasticity
bptest(second_stage)
```

## 3. Expected Findings
We expect the coefficient of x (Democratic control) to be positive, indicating that Democratic control is associated with higher public spending. The magnitude of the effect will depend on the strength of the relationship between Democratic control and public spending. The instrument, z (close-election Democratic win), should help isolate the causal effect of Democratic control on public spending by accounting for potential endogeneity.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use close-election Democratic wins as an instrument for Democratic control.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The analysis suggests a negative causal impact of Democratic control on public spending.
